html:
The Kaqchikel are a Maya people of the central highlands of Guatemala, between Guatemala City and Lake Atitlán. In 1492 they ruled one of the two main highland kingdoms.

They had been allies of the K'iche' but broke away around 1470 and founded their own capital at Iximche. The two kingdoms then fought each other, and the Kaqchikel also fought the Tz'utujil of Lake Atitlán. When Pedro de Alvarado arrived in 1524 the Kaqchikel kings welcomed him as an ally against the K'iche', and he set up the first Spanish capital of Guatemala at Iximche. His demands for gold soon drove them to revolt, and they fought the Spanish until about 1530.

The Annals of the Kaqchikels, written by Kaqchikel nobles in the 1500s and 1600s, tell their history from their own side. Kaqchikel is still spoken by several hundred thousand people. Their ancestors belong to the Maya world.
sum: The Kaqchikel are a Maya people of the central highlands of Guatemala, between Guatemala City and Lake Atitlán. In 1492 they ruled one of the two main highland kingdoms.
